docs.title: Lamia Studio
docs.text: Lamia Studio is a dedicated IDE for the Lamia programming language, built on top of VS Code. It provides syntax highlighting, code execution, debugging, and an AI-powered chat assistant for writing Lamia code.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Syntax highlighting for .lm and .hu files
  • AI Chat that understands Lamia syntax and can help with writing code with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and custom LLM adapters
  • One-click run and step-by-step debugging for .lm files
  • Go to definition, hover info, references, and completions for Lamia syntax elements and functions
  • Project model discovery — models from your config.yaml files appear in the chat model selector

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Download and install Lamia Studio
  2. Open IDE with "lamia ." from a project directory or by launching the "Lamia Studio"
  3. Open the chat panel (Cmd+Shift+L / Ctrl+Shift+L)
  4. Configure an API key (gear icon in chat header)
  5. Start asking questions or writing Lamia code

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Using Lamia Chat — the AI assistant built into the IDE
  • API Keys & Models — configure providers and select models

docs.title: Lamia Language Documentation
docs.text: For the Lamia language itself (syntax, web automation, validation, etc.), see the Lamia Language Docs.

docs.title: From the Chat Panel
docs.text:
1. Click the gear icon (⚙) in the chat header bar
  2. Select a provider (Anthropic or OpenAI)
  3. Paste your API key
  4. Click Save Key

The status line shows which providers are configured.

docs.title: Manual Configuration
docs.text:
API keys are stored in ~/.lamia/.env. You can edit this file directly:

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-api03-...
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

docs.title: Changing API Keys
docs.text: To update a key, simply click the gear icon (⚙) in the chat header bar, select the provider, and enter the new key.

docs.title: Selecting a Model
docs.text: Use the dropdown in the chat header bar. Models appear from three sources, in priority order:

docs.title: 1. Project Models (from config.yaml)
docs.text:
If your project has a config.yaml or multiple config.yaml files in case of multi project workspace, all models from the model_chain section are discovered and appear first:

model_chain:
  - name: "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
    max_retries: 3
  - name: "openai:gpt-4o"
    max_retries: 2

Lamia Studio discovers config.yaml files in your workspace (up to 4 directories deep) and the global ~/.lamia/config.yaml.

docs.title: 2. Built-in Model List (models.json)
docs.text:
After project models, Lamia Studio adds models from a built-in list. This list is fetched from the lamia-ide repository on startup, with a bundled copy as fallback.

Models whose provider has no configured API key show a lock icon (🔒). Configure the key to unlock them.

docs.title: Model Format
docs.text:
Models use the format provider:model-id, for example:

  • anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514
  • openai:gpt-4o
  • ollama:llama3

docs.title: Switching Models Mid-Chat
docs.text: You can switch models at any time using the dropdown. The next message will use the new model. The backend config is updated automatically.

docs.title: Custom Models
docs.text: Lamia Studio supports models beyond the built-in Anthropic and OpenAI options, including Ollama local models and custom LLM adapters.

docs.title: Ollama (Local Models)
docs.text:
To use local models via Ollama:

  1. Install and start Ollama on your machine
  2. Add the model to your project config.yaml:
model_chain:
  - name: "ollama:llama3"
    max_retries: 2
  1. The model will appear in the chat dropdown as llama3 (ollama).

No API key is needed for Ollama — it runs locally.

docs.title: Custom LLM Adapters
docs.text: Lamia supports custom LLM adapters for providers not built into the system. These are Python files placed in the extension/adapters/ folder of your Lamia installation or in your project. See Lamia Docs — Custom LLM Adapters for the adapter API and implementation guide.

docs.title: Creating an Adapter and registering
docs.text:
An adapter is a Python file that implements the Lamia LLM adapter interface. Place it in your project directory or the global adapters folder.

Add the adapter's provider to your config.yaml:

model_chain:
  - name: "my_custom_provider:my-model-v1"
    max_retries: 3

docs.title: API Keys for Custom Adapters
docs.text:
For custom providers that require API keys, add the key to ~/.lamia/.env:

# The LLM adapter implementation requires specifying the name of the API key name in the python file
MY_PROVIDER_API_KEY=your-key-here

docs.title: Using Lamia Chat
docs.text: The Lamia Chat panel is an AI assistant built into the IDE. It can answer questions about Lamia, generate Lamia projects from scratch, edit files in your projects, fix issues in your code, and more.

docs.title: Opening the Chat
docs.text:
• Press Cmd+Shift+L (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+L (Windows/Linux)
  • Or click the chat icon in the secondary sidebar

docs.title: Sending Messages
docs.text: Type your message in the text area and press Enter to send. Use Shift+Enter for a new line.

docs.title: Attaching Files
docs.text:
You can give the assistant context about specific files:

  • @-mention: Type @ followed by a filename to search project files and attach them
  • SHIFT button + Drag and drop: Drag files from the explorer into the chat input area (hold Shift while dragging)
  • Copy with context: When you copy code from the editor (Cmd+C), the file path and line numbers are automatically tracked and attached to your next message

docs.title: New Chat
docs.text: Click the + button in the chat header to start a fresh conversation. You always load the previous chats from the chat history.

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Click the clock icon in the chat header to browse previous conversations. Click any chat to reload it. Delete chats with the × button.

docs.title: Model Selection
docs.text: Use the model dropdown in the chat header to switch between available models.See API Keys & Models documentation about what models are available and how to add more models.

docs.title: Stop Generation
docs.text: Click the Stop button to cancel a response in progress. The input will be restored so you can edit and resend.

docs.title: Retry
docs.text: If a response fails, click the Retry button on the error message. If the assistant completed some steps before the error, it will continue from where it left off.

docs.title: Tool Usage
docs.text:
The assistant can use tools during a conversation.

Tool progress is shown as a step-by-step log with checkmarks (✓) or error indicators (✗).

docs.title: File Changes
docs.text:
When the assistant creates or modifies files, a summary appears below the response:

  • Created: new file was written
  • Modified: existing file was changed — click View Diff to see before/after, Open to jump to the file in the editor

docs.title: Code Blocks
docs.text:
Code snippets in responses have action buttons:

  • Copy — copy the code to clipboard
  • Insert — insert the code at the cursor position in the active editor

docs.title: Debugging .lm Files
docs.text: Lamia Studio includes a full debugger for .lm files with breakpoints, step-by-step execution, and variable inspection.

docs.title: From the Editor
docs.text:
1. Open a .lm file
  2. Click the debug icon in the editor title bar or right-click the file in the explorer and select Lamia: Debug Current File
  3. Or right-click the file in the explorer and select Lamia: Debug Current File

docs.title: From the Debug Panel
docs.text:
1. Open the Run and Debug panel (Cmd+Shift+D / Ctrl+Shift+D)
  2. Select Debug Lamia File from the dropdown
  3. Press the green play button

docs.title: From a Code Lens
docs.text: A Debug link appears at the top of .lm files. Click it to start debugging.

docs.title: Setting Breakpoints
docs.text: Click in the gutter (left margin) next to any line in a .lm file to set a breakpoint. A red dot appears. The debugger will pause execution at that line.

docs.title: Debug Controls
docs.text:
Once paused at a breakpoint, use the debug toolbar:

  • Continue (F5) — resume execution until the next breakpoint
  • Step Over (F10) — execute the current line and move to the next
  • Step Into (F11) — step into a function call
  • Step Out (Shift+F11) — run until the current function returns
  • Stop (Shift+F5) — terminate the debug session

docs.title: Inspecting Variables
docs.text:
While paused:

  • The Variables panel shows local and global variables
  • Hover over variables in the editor to see their values
  • Use the Debug Console to evaluate expressions

docs.title: Debug Configuration
docs.text:
The default configuration works for most cases. For custom setups, create a .vscode/launch.json:

{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "lamia",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Debug Lamia File",
      "program": "${file}",
      "cwd": "${fileDirname}",
      "stopOnEntry": false
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description Default program Path to the .lm file ${file} (current file) cwd Working directory ${fileDirname} (file's folder) stopOnEntry Pause on the first line false

docs.title: Writing .hu Files
docs.text: .hu (Human) files are plain-text prompt templates. They define instructions for an LLM in natural language, with parameter placeholders for dynamic content.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
A .hu file is plain text with single-brace parameter placeholders:

You are an expert code reviewer.

Review the following code for correctness, security, and performance issues.

Code to review:
{code}

Focus areas:
{focus_areas}

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Plain text only — no markdown (no **bold**, # headers, `backticks`, or HTML)
  • Single braces for parameters: {param_name} (double braces {{text}} become literal text with {text} value when sent to the LLM)
  • No output format descriptions — Lamia enforces output schemas and .hu files should be return type agnostic to be reusable.
  • Keep them concise — shorter prompts perform better

docs.title: Calling .hu Files
docs.text:
From a .lm file:

result = review_code(code=source_text, focus_areas="security") -> JSON[ReviewResult]

This calls review_code.hu, substitutes the parameters, sends it to the LLM, and parses the response as ReviewResult.

docs.title: IDE Features for .hu Files
docs.text:
• Syntax highlighting — parameters {name} are highlighted distinctly
  • Go to definition — Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click on a .hu filename in .lm code jumps to the file
  • Hover info — hover over a .hu call to see the template contents and parameters
  • Completions — parameter names suggested when calling .hu files

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
To quickly navigate between .lm and .hu files:

  1. In a .lm file, Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click on any .hu call to jump to it
  2. Use Ctrl+Shift+O / Cmd+Shift+O for document symbols — lists all functions and .hu calls
  3. Use Ctrl+P / Cmd+P and type .hu to find prompt files by name

For the full .hu syntax reference, see the Lamia Language Docs — .hu Syntax.

docs.title: Writing .lm Files
docs.text: .lm files are Lamia's executable files — they use Lamia syntax and can augment it with Python syntax for the actions that are not supported by Lamia syntax.

docs.title: IDE Features for .lm Files
docs.text:
• Syntax highlighting — Python + Lamia extensions highlighted correctly
  • Go to definition — Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click on .hu file calls to jump to the template
  • Hover info — hover over symbols for documentation
  • Code lens — Run and Debug links appear above the file
  • Completions — parameter names suggested when calling .hu files

For the full Lamia language reference, see the Lamia Language Docs.

docs.title: Running a .lm File
docs.text: There are several ways to run a .lm file:

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcut
docs.text: With a .lm file open, press Cmd+Shift+R (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+R (Windows/Linux).

docs.title: Play Button
docs.text: Click the play button (▶) in the editor title bar when a .lm file is open.

docs.title: Right-Click Menu
docs.text: Right-click a .lm file in the explorer and select Lamia: Run Current File.

docs.title: Code Lens
docs.text: A Run link appears at the top of every .lm file. Click it to execute.

docs.title: CLI Path
docs.text:
By default, Lamia Studio uses lamia from your PATH. To use a specific binary:

  1. Open Settings (Cmd+, / Ctrl+,)
  2. Search for lamia.cliPath
  3. Set the full path to your Lamia CLI executable if you want to change it

docs.title: IDE Settings
docs.text:
Lamia Studio settings are accessible via Cmd+, (macOS) or Ctrl+, (Windows/Linux). Search for "Lamia" or navigate to the "Extensions"->"Lamia" section to find all Lamia-specific settings.

Setting Description Default lamia.cliPath Path to the lamia CLI executable "lamia" (from PATH) lamia.chat.timeoutMs Timeout for chat responses in milliseconds 300000 (5 min)

docs.title: Chat Config
docs.text: Lamia Studio maintains ~/.lamia/ide/config.yaml for the chat panel's selected model. This file is auto-managed.

docs.title: File Locations Summary
docs.text: File Purpose ~/.lamia/.env API keys for LLM providers ~/.lamia/ide/config.yaml Chat panel selected model (auto-managed) ~/.lamia/ide/chats/<hash>/ Saved chat history (per workspace) <project>/config.yaml Project-specific model and provider config

docs.title: Project Configuration (config.yaml)
docs.text: Every Lamia project uses a config.yaml file to define which LLM models to use and how providers are configured.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: Lamia Studio discovers config.yaml files from workspace folder (and subfolders, up to 4 levels deep).

docs.title: How It Affects the Chat
docs.text:
• Models from model_chain appear at the top of the chat model dropdown
  • When you select a model in chat, Lamia Studio writes a separate chat config to ~/.lamia/ide/config.yaml (do not edit this file manually)

docs.title: Multiple Projects
docs.text: If your workspace contains multiple Lamia projects (subfolders with their own config.yaml), all discovered models are merged into the chat dropdown. When you switch to a file in a different project, the chat backend automatically switches to that project's working directory.

docs.title: First Steps
docs.text: After installing Lamia Studio, here is how to get productive quickly.

docs.title: 1. Open the Chat Panel
docs.text: Press Cmd+Shift+L (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+L (Windows/Linux) to open the Lamia Chat panel in the secondary sidebar.

docs.title: 2. Configure an API Key
docs.text: The chat assistant requires an LLM provider. Click the gear icon (⚙) in the chat header bar and enter your API key for Anthropic or OpenAI.

docs.title: 3. Create a Lamia Project
docs.text:
Create a folder with a config.yaml file. It is recommended to start with something simple like this:

model_chain:
  - name: "anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
    max_retries: 2

Then create your first .lm file. Start with the help of the chat assistant. Describe what you want to do and the chat assistant will write the first version of the code.

docs.title: 4. Run Your Code
docs.text: With a .lm file open, press Cmd+Shift+R (macOS) or Ctrl+Shift+R to run it. You can also click the play button (▶) in the editor title bar.

docs.title: 5. Ask the Chat for Fixes
docs.text: Type a question in the chat panel. The assistant can help with syntax, web automation, validation, and more. It can also read and edit files in your project.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Action macOS Windows/Linux Open Chat Cmd+Shift+L Ctrl+Shift+L Run .lm File Cmd+Shift+R Ctrl+Shift+R Debug .lm File Click bug icon or use debug menu Same Copy with context Cmd+C (in editor) Ctrl+C

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Q: What is the difference between Lamia Studio and VS Code?

Lamia Studio is a custom build of VS Code with the Lamia extension pre-installed and configured. It includes branding, default settings optimized for Lamia development, and the chat panel enabled by default.

Q: Can I install the Lamia extension in regular VS Code?

Yes. The extension can be packaged as a .vsix and installed in any VS Code instance:

  1. Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/lamia-lang/lamia-ide.git
  2. Install dependencies: cd lamia-ide/extension && npm install
  3. Compile: npm run compile
  4. Package: npx @vscode/vsce package --no-dependencies
  5. In VS Code, open the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P)
  6. Run "Extensions: Install from VSIX..." and select the generated .vsix file
  7. Reload VS Code

You will also need Python 3.10+ and the Lamia runtime (pip install lamia-lang).

Q: Where is the Lamia language documentation?

The language docs are at lamia-lang.github.io/lamia. The IDE docs (this site) cover the editor features.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
Q: Which LLM providers are supported?

Built-in support for Anthropic and OpenAI. Ollama and custom adapters are supported via config.yaml. See Custom Models.

Q: Are my API keys stored securely?

Keys are stored in ~/.lamia/.env as plain text. They are never leave your computer. Lamia does not have servers and does not collect any telemetry data.

Q: Can I use the chat without an API key?

Only if you have a local models configured. See Custom Models for more information. You need API keys only for cloud providers.

Q: Why does the model dropdown show a lock icon?

The lock (🔒) means no API key is configured for that model's provider. Click the gear icon to add one.

Q: Where are my chat conversations stored?

In ~/.lamia/ide/chats/<workspace-hash>/. Each chat is a JSON file. They persist across IDE restarts.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
Q: Can I run .hu files directly?

No. .hu files are prompt templates — they are called from .lm files. Use Go to Definition to navigate from a .lm call to its .hu file.

Q: How do I navigate from a .lm file to a .hu file?

Ctrl+Click / Cmd+Click on the .hu file name in your .lm code. The definition provider resolves it automatically.

Q: Does the debugger work with web automation?

Yes. You can set breakpoints and step through web.navigate(), web.click(), etc. The browser operations execute at each step.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Q: How do I reset everything?

Delete ~/.lamia/ to remove all config, keys, and chat history. On next launch, Lamia Studio will recreate the defaults.

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text: If you encounter a bug or unexpected behavior in Lamia Studio, please report it so we can fix it.

docs.title: Quick Report with System Info
docs.text:
Lamia Studio can automatically collect your system details to include in a bug report:

  1. Open the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P)
  2. Type "Lamia: Copy System Info for Bug Report" and select it
  3. A formatted text block is copied to your clipboard containing:
    • Lamia Studio version
    • Lamia CLI version
    • Operating system and version
    • Python version
    • Configured providers
    • Active extensions
    • Workspace info
  4. Paste this into your issue report

docs.title: Filing an Issue
docs.text:
1. Go to the Lamia IDE Issues page
  2. Click New Issue
  3. Use a descriptive title
  4. In the body, include:
    • What happened — describe the bug or unexpected behavior
    • What you expected — what should have happened instead
    • Steps to reproduce — how to trigger the issue
    • System info — paste the output from the command above
  5. If relevant, include screenshots or the error message from the chat panel
